articles.standfirst: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Real Madrid y al Málaga en el Santiago Bernabéu este domingo
articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Real Madrid y al Málaga en el Santiago Bernabéu este domingo
articles.body: El Real Madrid recibe al Málaga este domingo en un duelo entre dos realidades completamente opuestas tras el arranque liguero. Los de José Mourinho llegan lanzados después de sumar sus dos primeros triunfos de la temporada. Se impusieron 2-1 en su visita al Espanyol, con gol de Jude Bellingham y un tanto decisivo de Carlos Espí ya en el descuento, y firmaron después una auténtica exhibición en su estreno en el Bernabéu, goleando 4-1 a la Real Sociedad gracias a un hat-trick de Kylian Mbappé y un gol más de Vinícius. Favorito para el partido entre Real Madrid y Málaga El Málaga, por su parte, todavía no conoce la victoria en su regreso a Primera División. Cayó 2-0 en su debut ante el Atlético de Madrid en el Metropolitano y después empató 1-1 en casa ante el Deportivo, en un partido en el que solo pudo igualar el marcador desde el punto de penalti. Con el Real Madrid en un estado de forma arrollador y un Málaga que suma un único gol en sus dos primeros partidos, el favoritismo de los locales en las casas de apuestas es abrumador. Codere paga la victoria del Real Madrid a cuota 1.11, por 7.50 del empate y 20 del triunfo malacitano. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan se apoya en lo visto en los dos partidos anteriores de cada equipo. El Real Madrid ha encajado gol en sus dos partidos de esta temporada, algo que abre una rendija de esperanza para el Málaga, aunque la solidez defensiva blanca en el comienzo de la temporada ha sido netamente superior a la capacidad ofensiva de los andaluces, que solo han anotado un tanto, y de penalti, en sus dos primeros encuentros. Esa balanza tan desigual hace que el mercado de las apuestas deportivas se incline por el no. Codere paga esta opción a 1.65, por 2.1 del caso contrario. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta claramente hacia un partido con muchos tantos en el marcador. El Real Madrid ha sumado ocho goles en sus dos primeros partidos de liga, una media de cuatro por encuentro que confirma el nivel de pegada de su ataque bajo las órdenes de Mourinho. El Málaga, aunque mucho más discreto en ataque, ha visto cuatro goles repartidos entre sus dos primeros compromisos, lo que también apunta a un partido con anotaciones frecuentes, sobre todo teniendo en cuenta la diferencia de nivel entre ambos conjuntos. Codere sitúa la cuota del +3.5 goles totales a 1.85, por 1.88 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners también invita a pensar en un partido con mucho volumen de juego ofensivo por parte local. El Real Madrid ha generado un notable número de saques de esquina en sus dos primeros partidos, favorecido por su dominio absoluto del balón y por la necesidad de sus rivales de replegarse atrás para intentar contener su ataque, algo que previsiblemente también hará el Málaga este domingo. Los andaluces, por su parte, apenas han generado ocasiones claras por banda en sus dos primeros encuentros, mostrando un perfil mucho más discreto en este apartado. Con un Real Madrid que suele acumular córners cuando el rival se cierra atrás, Codere sitúa la cuota del +9.5 córners totales a 1.72, por 1.9 del caso contrario.

articles.title: Super League: Warrington seal home play-off spot as Wakefield also book post-season place
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves withstand late Hull FC fightback to win and guarantee home play-off; Wakefield Trinity beat York Knights to confirm their own post-season spot; watch round 26 of Super League from Thursday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Sam Burgess's side looked to be cruising to a sixth straight win after back-to-back tries from Leon Hayes and Matty Ashton put them well in control towards the end of the first half.

The hosts had more than matched their opponents in the opening stages and looked set to reach the interval level after Warrington captain George Williams and Hull's Aidan Sezer traded early penalties, but hesitation under two high kicks cost the home side dear and Warrington went in 10 points clear.

When Josh Thewlis crossed for Warrington's third try 10 minutes into the second half it looked all over, but the Black and Whites, playing their last home game of the season, belatedly stirred.

Quick converted tries from Ethan O'Neill and Tom Briscoe, who is preparing to bring his 17-year career to a close, thrust them back into contention and left the visitors clinging on to seal a top-four slot.

Victory may also have come at a price for Warrington after Aaron Lindop failed a head injury assessment while Burgess lost both Luke Thomas and Joe Philbin to apparent leg injuries.

"We controlled the game for large parts, and I was a bit disappointed that they were able to score two tries towards the end," said Burgess, speaking to Sky Sports .

"I'm proud of them, they're a joy to coach. We're getting tough which is an important part of our journey - to be able to manage these periods and just get on with the job."

Hull FC head coach Andy Last praised his side's fighting spirit and paid tribute to Briscoe, who shared some emotional moments with the supporters after the final whistle.

"I'm disappointed with the results but I'm really proud of the performance," he said. "We were up against a really good team who are in good form, and we went toe to toe with them for 80 minutes.

"Tom Briscoe, a remarkable performance for him today, and great that he was able to score that try in front of the home fans."

Wakefield see off York to join Wolves in the play-offs

Wakefield came on strong in the second half to beat struggling York 28-12 and guarantee a place in the post-season play-offs.

Daryl Powell's side had to survive a scare as the visitors briefly hauled level early in the second period before tries from Jayden Myers, Max Jowitt and Lachlan Walmsley got the job done.

Corey Hall's converted try put the hosts in front early and after former Wakefield player Ben Jones-Bishop reduced the deficit, Walmsley grabbed his first to carve out a six-point half-time lead.

Mark Applegarth's side responded well and pulled level through a brilliant run by Xavier Va'a and Jon Bennison's subsequent conversion, but York's good work was undone when Myers barged over from Mike McMeeken's short pass.

Bennison's ball was then intercepted, allowing Jowitt to effectively seal the contest before Walmsley put the gloss on the win with his second late on.

The result was a welcome boost for Wakefield after three straight defeats and moves them two points clear in fourth place and six above seventh-placed St Helens, with their hopes of securing a home play-off tie likely to hinge on next week's visit of Warrington.

Depleted Bulls stay bottom despite spirited fightback

Bradford Bulls' survival hopes are hanging by a thread after a 28-18 defeat in Toulouse left them two points from safety with two rounds remaining.

With 17 first-teamers unavailable, four of them hurt in the loss at Leigh eight days earlier and Loghan Lewis suspended, the 17 fit men were the 17 who travelled for head coach Kurt Haggerty – among them academy youngster Harvey Ward for a senior bow off the bench, though there was some relief in comebacks for vice-captain Ryan Sutton and wing Connor Wynne.

For 17 minutes, it threatened to unravel entirely. Cesar Rouge's boot kept turning the makeshift visitors around and by the time Paul Ulberg had barged his way over and Luke Polselli had finished off a three-on-one, sprung when Romeo Tropis slipped clear of Luke Hooley, the hosts led 10-0.

The response said everything about Bradford's night. Riley Dean carved Toulouse open to create a score for Chris Atkin, only for Ethan Quai-Ward to release John Toleafoa for a first try of the campaign that stretched the interval gap back to 10 at 16-6.

Dean was repelled twice on the line as Bradford pushed bravely while Sutton and Eliot Peposhi combined to keep Toleafoa out at the other end and once Maxime Stefani spilled possession, Andy Ackers sold a dummy and stepped his way over to make it a four-point game.

Toulouse settled it inside the last seven minutes, Mathieu Jussaume claiming his 16th try of the year before Tropis applied the finish to a flowing move, securing a ninth win of the season for the ninth-placed side and payback for their March loss in Yorkshire.

Alfie Leake at least gave the travelling contingent a final-whistle lift, the academy graduate grabbing a maiden senior try with a final act of defiance.

The equation for Bradford is now brutally simple they must beat 10th-placed Castleford at home on Thursday or the trip to second-bottom York Knights a week later could see the whole season on the line.

Toulouse close out against Hull FC on Friday and then at Warrington.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: Mets Activate Juan Soto From Injured List After 1-Month Absence
articles.summary: The New York Mets activated star outfielder Juan Soto from the injured list on Saturday after a one-month absence.
articles.body: The Juan the New York Mets invested $765 million in has returned. New York announced on Saturday afternoon that it has activated Soto from the 10-day injured list. Soto, who's batting second and serving as the Mets' designated hitter in their Saturday afternoon home matchup against the Houston Astros, hasn't played since July 24 due to a calf injury. To make room for Soto on the active roster, the Mets sent infielder Eric Wagaman to Triple-A Syracuse. Soto, a six-time Silver Slugger and five-time All-Star, also missed roughly three weeks in April due to a calf injury. Through 84 games this season (359 plate appearances), Soto has totaled 21 home runs, 52 RBIs, a 164 OPS+ and 2.7 wins above replacement, while boasting a .283/.408/.539 slash line. He ranks in the 93rd percentile of MLB in average exit velocity (92.5 mph), 92nd percentile in barrel percentage (14.3%) and 89th percentile in hard-hit percentage (48.6%), according to Statcast. As for the club he's returning to, the Mets have lost three consecutive games and four of their last five. New York is 60-75, good for 13th in the National League and last in the NL East. Soto, 27, is in the second season of an MLB-record 15-year, $765 million deal with the Mets.

articles.title: Hungarian Darts Trophy: Luke Humphries suffers shock defeat to Dirk van Duijvenbode as Michael van Gerwen delivers comeback win
articles.summary: Luke Humphries was beaten 6-3 in the second round in Budapest on his first European Tour appearance since March; Dirk van Duijvenbode advances to Sunday's finals day alongside compatriot Michael van Gerwen; Gian van Veen and Josh Rock both produced 6-0 victories on Saturday evening
articles.body:
With Luke Littler skipping the event, the world No 2 had arrived as the man to beat and in prime form after winning Wednesday's Players Championship event in Leicester, but his first European Tour outing since lifting the Belgian Darts Open title in March ended a day short of finals day.

Van Duijvenbode, a World Matchplay semi-finalist this summer, produced the flourish of the match with a 140 finish on tops-tops to move within a leg of victory before sealing his place in Sunday's Finals Day

Victory ended Van Duijvenbode's nine-match losing run against the world No 2, the Dutchman reeling off four consecutive legs from 3-2 adrift and averaging 98."

"Luke is a phenomenal player, but I think I'm okay as well," said Van Duijvenbode – a three-time runner-up on the European Tour circuit.

"I'm happier in life at the moment. I've had a lot of struggles, but I feel better, life is better and I'm getting better now hopefully."

Elsewhere, Michael van Gerwen recovered from 3-1 down to beat James Hurrell 6-4 and keep alive his bid for a second Hungarian Darts Trophy crown, sealing his place in Sunday's finals day.

He'll meet Nathan Aspinall in the last 16 after 'The Asp' defeated Ryan Joyce 6-4 despite being out-averaged, with five 180s and the greater volume of chances at a double carrying the 15th seed through.

Gian van Veen was imperious in whitewashing Hungarian qualifier Nandor Major 6-0, missing just three darts at a double in a finishing masterclass and converting a sublime 167 finish along the way.

Josh Rock also managed a 6-0 triumph as the Northern Irishman overcame an off-form Joe Cullen.

Fourth seed Jonny Clayton defeated home hope Laszlo Kadar, who stunned Daryl Gurney on Friday night, 6-3.

Keane Barry is also through after reeling off five consecutive legs to beat Madars Razma 6-2 and reach a first European Tour finals day in three years – although the Latvian left Budapest with the shot of the night, a 158 checkout completed on the bull.

Cross escapes again as defending champion Springer beaten

The tournament had already made history before the weekend, with Beau Greaves becoming the first woman to compete in a European Tour event on Friday and pushing 2018 world champion Rob Cross all the way to a deciding leg before losing 6-5.

Cross needed a second successive last-leg escape, surviving two 136 finishes and missed match darts from Luke Woodhouse before sealing a 6-5 win with a 130 checkout on the bull, a day on from his decider against Beau Greaves.

Earlier in the day, defending champion Niko Springer's reign ended as Ryan Searle beat him 6-4, in a match that lasted just 14 minutes. Searle pinned the bull for a 121 break on his way through and Springer's last chance went with a missed bull for a 164 checkout that would have forced a decider.

Gary Anderson made the statement of the afternoon, a first European Tour win of 2026 delivered in style as the two-time world champion averaged 105.27 in a 6-2 dismantling of Krzysztof Ratajski, while Dave Chisnall produced a ton-plus average of his own to dump out 13th seed Wessel Nijman 6-2.

Chris Dobey fought back from 4-0 down to beat Tom Sykes 6-5 and keep alive his pursuit of a maiden European Tour title, while Ross Smith averaged over 101 in beating William O'Connor 6-2.

Elsewhere, Jermaine Wattimena carried his Leicester title-winning form into a 6-4 win over Andrew Gilding and Danny Noppert survived six missed match darts before seeing off Ritchie Edhouse 6-4.

articles.title: Rays Set For New $2.3B Stadium Project After County, City Approve Financing Plan
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays have secured county approval for a financing plan to build a new stadium.
articles.body: The Tampa Bay Rays got county approval Friday on a financing plan that will allow them to build a new stadium, a day after city officials approved their part for the $2.3 billion ballpark project that will replace the domed Tropicana Field. The Hillsborough County Commission voted 5-2 on Friday to approve its $796 million share of the mixed-use entertainment district that includes a new 31,000-seat stadium that will be near Raymond James Stadium, home of the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Rays' new stadium is expected to open in 2029. The Tampa City Council city voted 4-3 on Thursday to approve $80 million. Rays CEO Ken Babby said the team’s partnership with the county and city on the project secures the long-term future of Major League Baseball in Tampa Bay. "We now look forward to celebrating before breaking ground with Hillsborough County and the City of Tampa on a future that has long been doubted, but will indeed happen," Babby said. "By making the Forever Home a reality, the Rays are now home forever in Tampa Bay." The Rays have committed to contributing at least $1.3 billion, plus any cost overruns. Another $30 million will come from federal disaster recovery funds. The Rays' ownership reached an agreement earlier this year with Hillsborough College to build the stadium and entertainment district on the campus and to renovate some of the school’s buildings. The property is located next to the New York Yankees’ spring training facility and across a highway from the NFL stadium. Since the team's inception in 1998, the Rays have played at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, except for moving home games to the Yankees’ George M. Steinbrenner Field in 2025 following hurricane damage at the Trop. The Rays’ lease runs through at least the 2028 season. The team returned to the Trop for the start of this season. A proposed $1.3 billion redevelopment deal for a new ballpark adjacent to the Trop fell through last year, raising new questions about the future of the team, which was bought last September by Patrick Zalupski’s ownership group. "This has been a long and challenging process, and we know that transformational projects rarely come easily," Zalupski said Friday. "Today’s vote represents an extraordinary milestone, not simply for the Rays or for a ballpark, but for the future of Tampa and the entire Tampa Bay region." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: How did the Rojiblanca academy get on against Pachuca?

articles.body:
Cantera Rojiblanca continues its journey in the 2026 Apertura, and this Saturday it was in action against Pachuca in the Matchday 6 fixtures of the tournament. Guadalajara managed to claim the extra point with its U-21 side after drawing 2-2 with the Tuzos and winning 5-4 in the penalty shootout, while the U-19 side tried to find a goal throughout its match but ultimately fell 5-0 to the team from Hidalgo.

We know that Chivahermanos always keep a close eye on the growth of our young Rojiblancos , so here are the results and highlights from the matches played by Guadalajara 's youth teams against Pachuca.

How did Cantera Rojiblanca fare against Pachuca?

Guadalajara 's U-21 side was involved in an exciting match against Pachuca at Field 5 of the Universidad del Futbol in the capital of Hidalgo, where the Rebaño played with intensity to rescue a draw. Just 3 minutes in, Anwar Ben Rhouma appeared to put Guadalajara ahead and give the Rojiblancos the lead. However, the home side responded, and in the 6th minute Anderson Rosales leveled the score, while in the 37th minute Cristóbal Hernández put the Tuzos in front before halftime.

Even so, the Rebaño did not give up and kept pushing for the equalizer throughout the second half. In the 82nd minute, Anwar Ben Rhouma made his presence felt again, taking a free kick that ended up in the back of the net to make it 2-2 and complete his brace. With these two goals, the Rojiblanco striker now has 4 goals in the tournament.

The draw sent the match to a penalty shootout, where Chivas prevailed 5-4 to earn the extra point.

articles.title: Liverpool one step closer to dream midfielder after Fabrizio Romano update
articles.summary: Liverpool are closing in on a dream midfielder after Fabrizio Romano's latest update. There has understandably been plenty of focus on Liverpool's attack in...
articles.body:
Liverpool are closing in on a dream midfielder after Fabrizio Romano's latest update.

There has understandably been plenty of focus on Liverpool's attack in the final days of the transfer window.

Richard Hughes is working to get a deal for Bradley Barcola over the line, and that pursuit could finally reach a successful conclusion in the coming days.

But Barcola is not the only attacking player on Liverpool's radar.

The Reds have also found themselves scrambling for a suitable option on the right wing. Ibrahim Mbaye had been under consideration for some time, with reports even suggesting that personal terms had been agreed.

More recently, however, Liverpool have broadened their search. Bids have been submitted for both Yankuba Minteh and Ismaila Sarr, only for those approaches to be rejected.

The need for a right-winger is obvious. Mohamed Salah left the club at the end of last season, leaving a huge void on that side of the pitch. Liverpool were always going to need to find a replacement.

What is harder to understand is why the search appears to have reached this stage so late in the window.

Liverpool would have known about Salah's impending departure months ago. There was plenty of time to prepare a clear recruitment strategy and identify multiple targets.

Much of the club's planning may have centred around Yan Diomande, but that cannot have been the only option. Once it became clear that he was not heading to Anfield, Liverpool should have been ready to move quickly onto the next name on the list.

That is what well-prepared recruitment departments do. Instead, with the window rapidly approaching its conclusion, Liverpool appear to be searching for solutions they should arguably have had lined up months ago.

Why Liverpool could still sign a midfielder

Liverpool have dithered for too long, failed to make decisive moves, and now find themselves in a desperate position heading into the final days of the transfer window.

But failing to sign a right-winger would not be their only mistake. Leaving the window without adding another midfielder could prove just as damaging.

Let's be honest: Liverpool's options in the middle of the pitch are looking increasingly thin.

With Curtis Jones now gone and Stefan Bajcetic expected to follow, these are the players realistically capable of operating in the double pivot:

James McConnell has not been included because he does not appear ready to make the step up just yet and is likely to leave on loan. Endo's future is also uncertain, with the Japanese midfielder potentially departing on a permanent basis before the deadline.

Nyoni is undoubtedly one of Liverpool's brightest young talents, but the club should not be placing too much responsibility on his shoulders at this stage of his development.

More importantly, Liverpool need a different profile in midfield.

The game against Newcastle highlighted exactly why. Andoni Iraola's system demands enormous discipline in the middle of the pitch. It requires someone who understands when to hold their position, when to protect the defence and when to commit forward.

Liverpool need a more defensively minded midfielder who can provide that balance.

It is something the recruitment team clearly recognises, with the club continuing to explore options. But, as has been the case elsewhere in the window, the concern is that Liverpool are once again leaving themselves with very little time to find the right solution.

One of the club's main targets who they have been in touch to sign all summer is Lamine Camara. Chelsea are also trying to sign the Senegalese midfielder.

Monaco are reluctant to sell but Liverpool might have just gotten a step closer.

Fabrizio Romano has shared that Monaco are signing Erik Lira, who is a Mexican midfielder.

That update opens the door for Camara, who would be a dream midfield addition, to leave Monaco and join Liverpool. But the Reds will need to act fast.

articles.title: Rybakina eases injury fears ahead of US Open
articles.summary: Australian Open champion Elena Rybakina says things are "all good" for the US Open after a heel injury forced her to retire from her Cincinnati WTA semi-fina...
articles.body:
Australian Open champion Elena Rybakina says things are "all good" for the US Open after a heel injury forced her to retire from her Cincinnati WTA semi-final last week.

"I started to practice, so I feel well," the Kazakh said Saturday. "We're still making some adjustments, but overall I'm happy how we dealt with the problem. We worked hard and likely it's all good right now and it's just a matter of a couple more practices and then, yeah, going on the match."

Rybakina can supplant Aryna Sabalenka atop the world rankings if she reaches the semi-finals at Flushing Meadows -- regardless of whether the Belarusian can win a third straight title.

For weeks she's said she isn't focused on the ranking, and her injury only reinforced that approach.

"From media mostly I know where I should get, how the others should play -- all the different scenarios," she said. "But for me, especially now when I had this injury last week, I feel like the most important (is) just try to stay healthy, play match at a time.

"I'm trying not to think about it at all and just play match at a time."

After hobbling out of her Cincinnati clash with Iga Swiatek, Rybakina said she didn't play for a week and saw several doctors.

"It wasn't easy because we didn't know exactly how the foot is gonna react, since it was very painful for me to go and serve on that match in Cincinnati ... then for a couple of days it was painful to even walk.

"After, we managed to do everything possible for it to get better, and I'm glad how the process is going for now."

Rybakina said fear of aggravating the injury won't hinder her in the final Grand Slam of the season.

"I'm quite confident with the decision we are making each day how to practice, what to do, and especially what can happen worst-case scenario.

"So all these things I feel quite confident."

articles.title: 2026 Little League World Series: Henderson, Nevada wins 2nd straight U.S. championship, will face international title winner Curaçao for LLWS trophy
articles.summary: Curaçao capitalized on Japan's defensive miscues, while Nevada just kept hitting against Ohio.
articles.body:
The 2026 Little League World Series championship will be determined on Sunday after Henderson, Nevada won the U.S. title and Curaçao took the international title. The teams will play on Sunday at 3 p.m. ET for the LLWS world title at Howard J. Lamade Stadium in Williamsport, Pennsylvania.

Hamilton, Ohio and Japan will play the third-place game at 10 a.m. ET.

Before an estimated crowd of 25,317, the team from Henderson, Nevada (representing the Mountain region) defeated Hamilton, Ohio (Great Lakes) for its second consecutive LLWS U.S. title with a 12-2 mercy rule win.

Nevada took a 1-0 lead in the first inning with a leadoff triple by pitcher Owen Guzman. He came in to score on an error by Ohio pitcher Josiah Infante who didn't catch the ball thrown back to the mound by catcher Boone Treadway. Infante escaped further damage by getting Brooks McFarland to ground into a double play.

Ohio tied the score at 1-1 in the second after a single from Bob Frazier. He scored on a groundball to shortstop that would have been a double play, but Nevada second baseman Adrian Cruz bounced the relay throw to first.

Nevada regained the lead in the second with a walk by Jace Ward and single from Michael Kleiner. Both runners moved to second and third on a wild pitch by Infante, then were driven in with a Maddox Bryan single.

Frazier took over to pitch for Ohio and walked Cruz. Bryan and Cruz were advanced on a sacrifice bunt by Payton Hinsen, then Carsynn Meyer hit an RBI single for a 4-1 lead. Nevada added 2 more runs on a Guzman single and wild pitch by Frazier.

Ohio mounted a rally in the fourth, putting its first two runners on with a Bryson Williams walk and Leo Feltner getting hit by a pitch. After Infante grounded into a double play, Frazier hit an RBI single to make it a 6-2 ballgame. A Xander Kinkade loaded the bases, but Guzman got Walker Osborne to fly out to center field to end the threat.

After adding 2 runs in the fourth, Nevada scored 4 more in the fifth with on a 2-run double by McFarland, an RBI groundout from Logan Edwards and a run-scoring single by Bryan to end the game with a 10-run lead.

Pitcher Jaymiëll Martina notched 12 strikeouts to lead Curaçao (Willemstad) to a 4-0 win over Japan (Tokyo) for the LLWS international championship.

Japan threatened to score early on singles by Tensei Yazawa and Yunosuke Yabe to lead off the game. Martina then walked Kei Kawanishi to load the bases. But Martina struck out Ryosuke Takaoka and Taiga Yumitori to keep Japan off the board.

Yunosuke Yabe didn't allow a hit in his first two innings for Tokyo. But Curaçao broke through with three runs in the third, thanks to several defensive miscues by Japan.

Jaymiel Antonia reached base on a dropped third strike by catcher Kei Kawanishi. Nathanael Jansen then laid down a bunt to move Antonia over, but Yazawa made an error throwing the ball to second base. Center fielder Takeru Yorozu then threw the ball wide of third base, allowing Antonia to score.

Jansen advanced to third on a sacrifice bunt, then came in to score on a bunt by Jordan Richards and an error by first baseman Rui Tobata. Curaçao added its third run when Tobata fielded another bunt and threw wide of first base, allowing Richards to score.

The LLWS schedule and results leading up to Saturday and Sunday's championship games can be seen here .

articles.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong pulls off what no Cubs player has done in 125 years
articles.summary: Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong made franchise history during a game against the Cincinnati Reds.
articles.body:
Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong may have solidified his case for National League MVP in one game. On Saturday against the Cincinnati Reds, Crow-Armstrong exploded. He went 4-for-6 at the plate, launching three home runs in a 17-5 win, collecting six RBIs and 13 total bases.

His numbers this year have continued to climb after a slow start. The 24-year-old now owns a .282 batting average, .377 on-base percentage, .944 OPS, 36 home runs and 89 RBIs across 136 games.

He has also swiped 36 bags and is widely regarded as the best defensive player in the league. Saturday's game was special and a clear indicator that he is emerging as one of the faces of baseball. It also placed him in Cubs history.

"Pete Crow-Armstrong is the youngest Cub since 1901 to have a 3HR game," wrote Cubs sideline reporter Taylor McGregor on X.

Crow-Armstrong's performance also gives him a shot at becoming the first Cubs player ever to post a 40-40 season. He is just four home runs and eight stolen bases away from the mark, with about four weeks remaining in the regular season. There is plenty of time to get there.

Crow-Armstrong is certainly taking time to enjoy his breakout season, but his eyes are set on much more. The Cubs are positioned to make a deep run in the MLB playoffs, and with him leading the charge they should feel confident they can compete for the World Series for the first time in a decade.

articles.summary: The New York Mets have placed outfielder Luis Robert Jr. on waivers, according to SNY's Anthony DiComo. The 29-year-old has seen limited action this season d...
articles.body:
The New York Mets have placed outfielder Luis Robert Jr. on waivers, according to SNY's Anthony DiComo. The 29-year-old has seen limited action this season due to injury issues , but has shown some pop since returning in July.

*Note: All stats entering play on Saturday, 8/29

The Mets acquired Robert Jr. in a trade with the Chicago White Sox this past January. He spent his first six seasons on the South Side and garnered several accolades in his time there. These include a Gold Glove in 2020, plus an All-Star nod and a Silver Slugger Award in 2023. He also finished as the runner-up for American League Rookie of the Year in the COVID-shortened 2020 season.

Robert Jr. made some noise to start his Mets tenure, including hitting a walk-off home run in April. However, he then went on the injured list with a lumbar disc herniation, causing him to miss nearly three months. Upon his return in late July, it was thought that Robert Jr. could be traded elsewhere at the deadline . This speculation mirrored several previous seasons for him, as he was often touted as a potential deadline chip with the White Sox, although they never pulled the trigger until this past offseason.

The Mets ultimately decided to keep Robert Jr. past August 3, even though his play since returning seemed to increase his trade value. Since his return just after the All-Star break, he has a slash line of .233/.296/.476 with eight homers and 15 RBI across 32 games.

If another team picks up Robert Jr., they'd presumably be adding him at the right time while his power is up. If he clears waivers, perhaps he will find his way back to the Mets roster before the end of the season. However, Robert Jr. getting claimed by another team would be a better outcome for both that team and the Mets. Whatever pop he can provide for the Mets won't get them any closer to the postseason at this point, and freeing up a roster spot will probably allow them one more September call-up than they would use otherwise.

If a contending team claims Robert Jr., they will be getting a versatile player who has a lot to offer both at the plate and in center field. Although his health is a concern, his assets make him one of the more notable players to watch on the waiver wire as the stretch run begins.

articles.title: Ja Morant Gives Hype Reaction To Damian Lillard’s Viral Workout Video
articles.summary: Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant does not hold back after Damian Lillard's impressive shooting display.
articles.body:
It's been a difficult stretch for Ja Morant . After a scandal ruined his reputation and derailed his NBA career, he's been working to claw his way back to restore what he lost.

Now that he's on the Portland Trail Blazers , expectations are low for the young point guard, but there are signs that something special is brewing. This latest sign came from Blazers legend Damian Lillard , who was captured making 1,110 out of 1,168 of his shots in a recent workout. Keep in mind that this comes on the heels of his Achilles tear in 2025, which kept him out of action for the entire 2025-26 campaign.

Lillard was once the face of the Trail Blazers and widely recognized as one of the best guards in the league . Known for his shooting, playmaking, and clutch scoring, Lillard holds the title as the greatest Blazer ever with career averages of 25.1 points, 4.3 rebounds, 6.7 assists, 1.0 steals, and 0.3 blocks per game on 43.9% shooting.

Between injuries and natural aging, we can't expect Dame to play at the level he was in his prime, but he can still make a huge difference if he's able to stretch the floor and help run the offense for his team. Judging by the latest video evidence, Lillard should have no issues contributing, and it's building excitement in Ja Morant, who responded to the clip with uncanny confidence.

Ahead of his first season in Portland, Morant isn't sure what to expect. He knows as much as anyone that they won't be in the title mix, especially after the injury to Shaedon Sharpe . Even so, they can make some noise if he returns to All-Star form.

With averages of 19.5 points, 3.3 rebounds, 8.1 assists, 1.0 steals, and 0.3 blocks per game last season, Ja's stats were down across the board as the Grizzlies struggled to stay competitive, but there's reason to believe he'll see better days in Portland. With a fresh start on a fringe playoff team, he can play freely without the added pressure of fan expectations. It won't hurt, either, to have Damian Lillard as a mentor and guide in the locker room.

For Ja, the most important thing is to stay on his best behavior and avoid any off-court drama. If he can keep his head down for at least a few years, it will go a long way toward restoring his fractured reputation. After such a checkered past, many are better against Morant, but the vibes are looking good on the Trail Blazers.

Between Lillard, Morant, Scoot Henderson , Donovan Clingan , and Deni Avdija , they have the talent and depth to secure a top-six seed next season and take that next step as a developing team. It will take time to bring everyone together, but Ja has already embraced the challenge, and he's eager to set things right after such a dark period.

articles.title: Five takeaways from UVA football’s dominant 34-8 win over NC State
articles.summary: Analyzing Virginia's dominant season-opening win against the Wolfpack in front of the first sold-out Stadium since 2008.
articles.body:
The Virginia Cavaliers were supposed to play their season-opener in a stadium 4,700 miles away. When the Rio de Janeiro deal collapsed in June and the ACC relocated the opener to Charlottesville, it's hard to imagine the Virginia administration could have pictured a better outcome than what happened Saturday. With ACC Huddle (the ACC's premier football show) in town and Shaquille O'Neal DJing a pregame concert for students, Virginia got something better than a novelty kickoff: a sold-out Scott Stadium, the first since the 2008 season opener against USC.

Rumor has it UVA made a big push to get 2027 high school recruits in the building for Saturday's game, and the ones on hand got a good look at what the place sounds like when it's full.

NC State was projected to be one of Virginia's tougher opponents this year, and the Cavaliers were only a 3.5-point favorite at kickoff — the line had opened at 5.5 and drifted toward the Wolfpack all week. The Wahoos showed early that they meant business, taking a 17-0 lead into halftime. They finished off a dominant 34-8 win, out-gained NC State 413-168, and held the ball for 38 minutes and three seconds.

Here are five takeaways from the opener.

The UVA defense hasn't changed a bit, and it didn't even have Kam Robinson

Virginia's defense finished last season as the reason the Cavaliers played for an ACC championship. It opened this one the same way, and it did it without its best player.

Kam Robinson was a game-time decision after tearing his ACL against Duke on Nov. 15 — a game UVA won 34-17, and one Robinson never should have gone back into. It was a devastating blow that no doubt played a role in Virginia's ACC Championship Game loss. He didn't dress Saturday. The 'Hoos only allowed 168 total yards anyway.

NC State was dominated at the line of scrimmage, running 24 times for 76 yards, an average of 3.2 a carry, and never finding a second gear on early downs. CJ Bailey, a highly touted third-year starter whom CBS Sports rated the No. 2 quarterback in the ACC this preseason, went just 12-of-23 for 84 yards with an interception. Add Will Wilson's relief work and the Wolfpack finished 15-of-27 for 92 yards through the air — 3.4 yards per attempt. NC State managed only ten first downs and punted seven times, giving Jackson Waller the busiest afternoon of anyone in a red jersey.

Myles Brown led with eight tackles, Maddox Marcellus added seven, and the front generated three tackles for loss. If there's a caveat on the defense, it's that Virginia managed only two sacks — a low number for a unit that played with a lead and had plenty of chances to tee off. Bailey had time in the pocket more often than the box score suggests. That's fixable for a defense that came on so strong in the second half of the 2025 season, especially when the coverage is this good, but it's worth watching.

Brandyn Hillman came home and took the ball away twice

Tony Elliott has been open about the one that got away. Hillman, a Churchland High School product out of Portsmouth, was the No. 4 player in Virginia in the 2023 class, and Elliott recruited him hard before Michigan won out. "I wanted him bad out of high school," Elliott said this offseason. "I just didn't have enough firepower." Eleven wins later, he had enough.

Hillman spent Saturday collecting both of Virginia's takeaways. The first came off a Fisher Camac deflection that hung in the air long enough for Hillman to run underneath it. The second was a punch-out on Bailey that Landon Danley fell on. Both were turning points, especially the punch-out, which was not only perfectly placed but stopped a near-certain NC State scoring drive in the red zone.

The secondary around him was every bit as good. Virginia broke up six passes as a unit. Jacobie Henderson had two of them and came within a step of an interception and a potential pick six, dropping into a throwing lane Bailey clearly didn't expect to be occupied. Batted balls at the line, contested throws downfield, and receivers running out of room left a highly touted NC State passing attack without answers all afternoon.

The most impressive sequence of the game had nothing to do with a highlight play. Virginia put together a 23-play drive, a school record, and by the end of it NC State's front seven was standing with hands on hips waiting for the next snap. For context, the longest drive of last season was 19 plays in the Gator Bowl.

Virginia physically dominated the game and flat out wore down the NC State defense by pounding the rock. UVA ran 57 times for 258 yards. It converted all four of its fourth-down attempts. It held the ball for 38:03 against 21:57, nearly doubling the Wolfpack's time of possession.

Virginia was 3-for-14 on third down, a number that would sink most teams but barely registered here, because Elliott kept sending the offense back out on fourth down and the line kept converting in short-yardage scenarios.

Beau Pribula is a dual threat, and the backfield is a committee

J'Mari Taylor carried a bellcow's workload last season and turned it into an undrafted free agent deal with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Finding one player to replace him was always going to be close to impossible. It's clear Virginia isn't trying to.

Jekail Middlebrook is the lead back. He had 15 carries for 64 yards, the early-down grinder the offense leaned on to set up everything else. But Xavier Brown was the most dangerous man in the group, going for 40 yards and a score on eight carries and then catching two balls for 58 yards and another touchdown, including a 45-yarder up the seam out of the backfield on a read option that fooled the Wolfpack secondary. Xay Davis punched in a short touchdown. Noah Vaughn got six carries. Peyton Lewis, the Tennessee transfer and another Virginia kid Elliott had chased out of high school, didn't enter until the second quarter and finished with 10 yards on six attempts.

The leading rusher, though, was the quarterback. Pribula carried 15 times for 110 yards at 7.3 a pop with a long of 22. It was clear early that this is a major part of the offense Virginia OC Des Kitchings has planned for this year, and a quarterback with that kind of running ability is a weapon. It's also 15 carries in Week 0 for a player Virginia cannot afford to lose. Plenty of Virginia fans watched through their fingers after a few massive hits that left Pribula visibly shaken.

That said, the stable of running options looks deep to start the season, and the intensity was on display. Every back finished runs. Nobody went down on first contact when a second effort was available.

The passing game is the one thing to be nervous about

Pribula's line looks terrific: 9-of-11, 155 yards, two touchdowns, no interceptions, 14.1 yards per attempt.

The number to sit with is 11. Virginia threw the ball just 11 times in roughly 68 snaps. Most of what worked came off play action, where the run game had linebackers so far downhill that the throws were nearly free — a 47-yard touchdown to Da'Shawn Martin, the 45-yarder to Brown. Kitchings also showed off more creativity with a rollout and a flea flicker.

At times Pribula looked reluctant to let it go, taking the check-down or tucking it when a receiver had a step. While that's an understandable instinct for a quarterback making his first start of the year with a big lead and an offensive line winning every snap, it's a genuine question in a game where Virginia has to throw to stay in it.

Luckily Virginia has a manageable schedule to start the season, but if the Cavaliers want to realize their goal of competing for an ACC championship, it's worth asking whether this is a viable formula against the best teams in the conference and the nation.

For now, there's reason to be cautiously optimistic.

Bonus: Will Bettridge gives Elliott the whole field

Bettridge opened the scoring with a 47-yarder, matching his longest of last season, and finished 2-for-2 on field goals and 4-for-4 on extra points for 10 total points. A kicker Elliott can trust from the mid-40s gives him more options later in the season. Daniel Sparks was also excellent when he was needed, averaging 45.4 yards on five punts with a long of 63.

Virginia has a bye before hosting Norfolk State on Friday, Sept. 11. This is a valuable extra week for a team that just ran the ball 57 times, and more importantly another two weeks of rehab for Kam Robinson before West Virginia comes to Charlottesville on Sept. 19 for the next real test.

Week 0 results get over-read every year. But this wasn't a fluky win over an overmatched opponent. NC State was a legitimate ACC team that oddsmakers thought could win in Charlottesville, and Virginia physically overmatched them. If the line plays like that and the defense keeps taking the ball away, this team will be in the ACC title conversation all the way through November.

articles.title: Lowe’s returns to help sponsor Jimmie Johnson in his final NASCAR race
articles.summary: Johnson will carry the familiar Lowe’s colors one final time when he drives the No. 48 in the 2027 Daytona 500
articles.body:
The upcoming 2027 Daytona 500 appearance for Jimmie Johnson will be a memorable one, no matter what happens on the track. The seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion will make his 703rd career start and his 24th appearance in the Daytona 500. He will be driving for the team he co-owns, piloting the No. 48 Legacy Motor Club Toyota.

It will be Johnson's last-ever Cup race in a career at the highest level that dates back 25 years. He has already worked it out with Rick Hendrick to drive the No. 48 in that race – the very number he won each of 83 Cup wins with. Previously, he's used the No. 84 in all of his starts with Legacy Motor Club.

On Saturday at Daytona, Johnson revealed that he will also have a familiar sponsor on the door of his No. 48, as Lowe's Home Improvement makes an unexpected return to NASCAR to sponsor Johnson in his farewell race.

Lowe's was the primary back for Johnson throughout most of his Cup career, before exiting the sport following the 2018 season. When Johnson won each of his seven Cup titles, it was a Lowe's No. 48 he drove to the championship stage.

Lowe's will share the car with Carvana and Ally, and Johnson should be locked into the race via the Open Exemption Provisional.

"When I first called Rick (Hendrick) about the idea he was in immediately," said Johnson. "I still knew there was a lot of work to be done with Lowe's, Ally, Carvana and all these pieces and how it would play out. But Mr. Hendrick's commitment to speak to everyone at Lowe's, looping in our existing partners and obviously Toyota's support – once the snowballs started rolling, it all came together. The neat thing is we've got a lot of time between now and the Daytona 500 to continue to amplify this opportunity."

Johnson, who turns 51 next month, is a two-time winner of the Daytona 500 (2006 and 2013). He took the No. 48 he will drive next February for a ceremonial lap around the track before the start of Saturday night's Cup race.

articles.title: Right side comes up big for Arizona volleyball in victory over Tarleton State
articles.summary: Arizona is out to a 2-0 start to the season
articles.body:
Women's volleyball relies heavily on the left side for its scoring, but Arizona needed some time for its outsides to get going on Saturday afternoon. The middles and right sides stepped up to lead the Wildcats to a 3-0 (25-17, 25-23, 25-22) victory over Tarleton State in the Wildcat Classic.

After one set, Destiny Ndam-Simpson and Carlie Cisneros had one kill apiece. Both were hitting .000. Opposite Kennedy Osunsanmi and middle blocker Marina Vosloo teamed up with the Wildcat servers to control the set anyway.

"That's part of our game plan is to be able to spread the offense a little bit," said Arizona head coach Rita Stubbs . "You know, it was hard for Carlie to score in the beginning, but she turned it on. Same thing that happened yesterday."

Both left sides eventually found their way, but it took a while and their efficiency took a hit. Ndam-Simpson ended with seven kills, two aces, nine digs, and two total blocks. She hit .217. Cisneros had six kills, five digs, and one solo block. She hit .111.

Osunsanmi never let down. Fellow opposite Renee Jones also pitched in to help Arizona pull out the win over a the Texans. The middles did their part throughout the match, as well.

"I'm just making sure I'm ready for every ball…and that (Maria Olga Siapani) knows I'm available," Osunsanmi said.

Osunsanmi tied Ndam-Simpson for the team lead with seven kills. She added three digs and four total blocks (one solo). Her 9.5 points also tied Ndam-Simpson for the team lead.

Jones have five kills on .333 hitting and one total block.

Arizona's starting middles made a statement. Journey Tucker had four kills and five total blocks. Two of her blocks were solo. Her 7.5 points were just behind Osunsanmi and Ndam-Simpson.

Freshman middle Marina Vosloo followed up her strong debut with another good outing, although she didn't play the whole match as Stubbs worked to get time for her bench. Vosloo had three kills on five swings without an error. She added an ace for four points. She left the match in the second set and did not return.

Getting the other players time on the court paid off in a big way for reserve middle blocker Kristen Dear . Dear had four kills on .800 hitting. The hitting percentage led all players who had more than one attempt. Despite playing just one set, she tied for second on the team with four total blocks. Two of those were solo, which tied Tucker for the team high in solo blocks.

"It was really nice seeing Kristen go out there and make a difference as a blocker as well as an attacker," Stubbs said. "All the middles are different. So one of the things is if you don't know which middle's out there, you don't really know who to prepare for or how to prepare."

Getting scoring from all parts of the court is what the Wildcats are working towards. Despite meeting that goal and closing it out in straight sets, the match wasn't easy for Arizona.

Tarleton State has had a strong weekend. They pushed UCSB to five sets on Friday. They had leads late in two of the three sets against Arizona. The Texans' final leads were 22-21 in the second and 18-16 in the third.

"I think they're doing a phenomenal job," Stubbs said. "And I told (head coach Jazmyne Johnson), I said, let's make sure we talk after this because your team is doing all the right stuff."

The second set was especially difficult for the Wildcats as the Texans kept them from getting into their offense smoothly. Aside from two overpasses, Arizona was generally able to recover on its way to salvaging the set.

"I thought they did a phenomenal job of having an idea of who to serve, and they kept pace on the ball," Stubbs said. "And when you do that, then we just got to be ready to respond. But I love the fact that we stayed together. At no point did we act like we were panicked. I don't know what was going on on the inside, but at no point did we like lose our mind or freak out that we couldn't do what was necessary."

The Wildcats also kept pressure on Tarleton State with the serve. Arizona had seven aces with six of those coming in the opening set. Ndam-Simpson, Siapani, and Brenna Ginder all ended with two each.

Stubbs is hoping to get the Wildcats in the top four of the Big 12 for attendance this season a year after finishing sixth. Arizona only has three nonconference matches at home this year, but it's off to a good start for attendance. The team drew 1,812 on Friday night and followed it with 2,026 on Saturday for a total of 3,838 over two days. Last year, UA drew a total of 2,999 in its first two matches.

articles.title: Stanford vs Hawai'i season opener: Live updates plus winners, losers
articles.summary: The Stanford Cardinal host the Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors in their college football season opener. Check out live updates, including winners and losers.
articles.body:
PALO ALTO, CA ― Stanford football is back as the Cardinal kick off their 2026 season in the ACC against the Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors at Stanford Stadium.

This season marks a new era for Stanford football as newly hired head coach Tavita Pritchard makes his debut.

The Cardinal hired Pritchard after the 2025 season to become the 37th head coach in the program's history. Pritchard, a 2009 graduate of Stanford, was previously a quarterbacks coach for the Washington Commanders .

The Cardinal are looking to improve upon last season's record when they finished with a 4-8 overall record, including 3-5 in the ACC.

Pritchard was a direct hire made by football general manager Andrew Luck. The former No. 1 pick in the 2012 NFL Draft joined the staff in 2024.

"Winning in college football today requires a leader of men who can build and motivate teams, recruit future stars, and develop and connect with talent," Luck said in a university statement . "Tavita Pritchard is exactly the right head coach at the right time to help us build on the foundation of this season and lead Stanford football to its next great era."

Hawai'i is coming off its best season since 2019, finishing with a 9-4 record. It concluded the 2025 season with a 35-31 win against California in the Sheraton Hawai'i Bowl.

The Rainbow Warriors start their season against another ACC opponent. These teams are facing each other for the third time in the last four years. This game is the tiebreaker between the two until their next meeting in 2030.

In their last matchup, Hawai'i got the upper hand on Stanford, winning 23-20 on a Kansei Matsuzawa's walk-off field goal in their 2025 season opener. The teams didn't play in 2024 but Stanford got a 37-24 win during Hawai'i's 2023 home opener.

USA TODAY Sports will provide live updates in the game, including winners and losers from today's matchup between Stanford Cardinal and Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors:

Who has the best helmet in college football? We rank the top 25

Hawai'i's offense picked up steam in the second quarter, especially the Rainbow Warriors' passing game. In eight plays they picked up 55 yards and a pitch to DeVon Rice for a three-yard score put Hawai'i on the board for the tie, 7-7.

Stanford's offense continues to put pressure on the Rainbow Warriors. The Cardinal took a 14-7 lead with 7:02 remaining in the first half. Davis Warren targeted Atticus Joseph on a slant route six-yards into the end zone as he caught the pass for the score.

Hawai'i's defense can't get a stop. Stanford continues rolling as they've scored on 50% of their offensive possessions.

Battle in the trenches: The Rainbow Warriors are losing the battle at the line. The Stanford defense has constantly applied pressure forcing Hawai'i to pass and make quick decisions before the play develops. They're run game has been obsolete.

Stanford Cardinal break the game open on their second possession of the game, driving downfield 89 yards which was capped by a 2-yard score by running back Micah Ford. The Cardinal lead 7-0 with 8:37 remaining.

Hawai'i's offense: The Rainbow Warriors can't seem to get anything going and have registered only three total offensive yards. They've been limited through the air and on the ground.

images.caption: Who has the best helmet in college football? Here's a look at the 25 best the sport has to offer heading into the 2026 season. (Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch)

NO. 25 OKLAHOMA . Oklahoma's interlocking "OU" is synonymous with one of the most successful programs in college football history, a logo worn by the likes of Billy Sims, Lee Roy Selmon, Brian Bosworth and, more recently, Adrian Peterson and Baker Mayfield. When paired with a shiny crimson helmet, it's one of the best looks in the sport. (Kyle Ross, IMAGN IMAGES)

NO. 24 ALABAMA . A look synonymous with college football, Alabama has a simple yet beautifully done design with player numbers. Adorning Alabama helmets since the 1950s, the Crimson Tide haven't changed their look much since then, and don't need to. It makes every player stand out while not messing with tradition. A major flex is using the helmet as a logo and the number representing the total national championships, which is at 18 claimed titles. Some teams have done their own versions of adding player numbers to helmets, but it's a design you always associate with the Crimson Tide. (Jeff Hanisch, USA TODAY Sports)

NO. 23 WYOMING . The flagship university in the Cowboy State, fittingly, has a cowboy as its mascot and with it, an incredible, distinct logo — a silhouette of a cowboy riding a bucking horse. The image, Bucking Horse and Rider, is actually a registered trademark of the state of Wyoming. The university says it represents "the toughness, and the never-say-die spirit that is Wyoming" and, just as important, it looks awfully good on a helmet. (Troy Babbitt, USA TODAY Sports)

NO. 22 BOISE STATE . The non-Power darling does a great job of using a great logo with an oversized look of the Bronco. Oversized logos on helmets usually look good, but this one stands out with how intense it is, especially how Boise State does a nice touch of really making the eye stand out. It could use it on both sides, but it still comes across perfectly on one. No matter what color the helmet or decal is, it works every single time. It's intense and fierce, matching the tenacity that comes with the blue turf. (Mark J. Rebilas, USA TODAY Sports)

NO. 21 WASHINGTON STATE . Wazzu has one of the best logos in college sports, a cougar head created by Randall Johnson in 1936 that spells out the school's initials, "WSU." It has become an iconic symbol for the university and in the broader college football world, thanks in some part to Ol' Crimson, a Washington State flag that has been in the background of every episode of "College GameDay" since 2003. (Petre Thomas, IMAGN IMAGES)

NO. 20 NEBRASKA . The Cornhuskers became a powerhouse when it added the block "N," and while there's nothing special about it, the helmet still is among the most recognizable. Nebraska has tried different variations with black that have mostly looked decent, but it further proves there is no need to mess with good ol' reliable. (Jeff Hanisch, IMAGN IMAGES)

articles.title: After fast start, Houston Astros' bats go quiet for long stretch in loss to New York Mets
articles.summary: Houston's offense was throttled by Mets starter Nolan McLean, who cruised through seven innings as New York evened the three-game series.
articles.body:
NEW YORK - Jeremy Peña strode to the plate and staged an ambush. Nolan McLean started Saturday's game at Citi Field with a four-seam fastball. Peña lined it into the left-field corner and sprinted to third base when the carom kicked past Brett Baty.

One pitch produced the Houston Astros ' first hit against the Mets' right-hander. McLean faced his next 18 hitters without allowing another. A day after their ace delivered a dominant outing , the Astros were subjected to one.

McLean spun seven innings of one-run ball against Houston, which could not recover in a 6-2 loss. Its lineup totaled four hits. The Mets struck 11 against the four pitchers they deployed in bullpen game, building a lead against bulk reliever Cristian Javier.

The Astros fell back to .500, at 68-68, with their division lead at 1 ½ games pending the Rangers' result. McLean handed a 4-1 lead to his bullpen. Yordan Alvarez, who had two of the Astros' hits, pared it with his 37th home run of the season in the eighth inning.

Francisco Alvarez countered with a two-run double off Kai-Wei Teng in the bottom of the inning. Mets center fielder A.J. Ewing robbed Christian Walker of potential extra bases with a catch against the wall with a runner on second in the ninth. The Astros totaled three at-bats with a man in scoring position.

a-struck out for Vázquez in the 8th. b-popped out for Pache in the 8th.

E_Baty (8). LOB_Houston 5, New York 7. 2B_Peña (16), Altuve (18), Lindor (9), Baty (17), F.Alvarez (12). 3B_Young (3). HR_Y.Alvarez (37), off Duarte. RBIs_Y.Alvarez 2 (93), Young 3 (35), Soto (53), F.Alvarez 2 (33). SB_Semien (10). SF_Y.Alvarez. S_Ewing.

Runners left in scoring position_Houston 1 (Trammell); New York 5 (Baty, Lindor 2, Semien 2). RISP_Houston 0 for 3; New York 4 for 12.

ABS Challenge_Sousa (Ball-Overturned to Strike); Varsho (Strike-Overturned to Ball).

Pitch timer violations_Javier (pitcher).

Umpires_Home, Carlos Torres; First, Nate Tomlinson; Second, Mark Wegner; Third, Jacob Metz.

McLean matched his longest outing of a season in which he owns a 3.06 ERA in 27 starts. He entered ranked 11th among qualified major-league starters in strikeout percentage and seventh in opponents' batting average. He notched four strikeouts in his seven innings but yielded just two hits.

Peña's set up a sacrifice fly from Alvarez, the run unearned given Baty's error. A sixth-inning single by Alvarez was the only other hit against McLean, who walked three but did not allow a Houston runner into scoring position after Peña in the first.

"He's tough," Astros manager Joe Espada said. "Sinker, cutter, kept us off-balance. Outside of that first inning we just couldn't do much against him. But I thought our at-bats continued to be competitive."

McLean led with three types of fastballs. He induced just six whiffs on 40 swings, but Houston hitters averaged only an 87.6 mph exit velocity against him. They did not hit a ball that reached an outfielder over a four-inning stretch before the sixth.

McLean barely needed to throw the curveball that has been arguably his best pitch, generating a .109 average and a 40.4% whiff rate before Saturday. He totaled seven curveballs on 93 pitches. Seventy-six were sinkers, cutters or four-seam fastballs. The Astros could not solve any of them.

Yordan Alvarez matches career high in HRs

Alvarez started the day leading or tied for the American League lead in all three Triple Crown categories, but his pace has slowed in August. Junior Caminero of the Rays hit his 36th home run Saturday, briefly tying Alvarez for the league lead. Pete Alonso began the day tied with Alvarez at 91 runs batted in.

Alvarez had one home run and nine RBIs in his first 24 games this month, a stretch in which he still had an .874 OPS. A two-hit day Saturday, including his 37th home run of the season, left him sporting a .320 average and 1.048 OPS.

"If the home runs are not there, you've still got to try to find a way to contribute and try to find a way to get on base," Alvarez said, through interpreter Otto Loor. "And that's what I've been trying to do."

With his 37th home run, Alvarez matched the career high he set in 2022. He did so with a laser. Daniel Duarte threw him a 1-1 cutter. Alvarez laced it 436 to right-center field at 113.4 mph off the bat. It was his fourth-longest homer of the season; the three longest were all hit at Globe Life Field.

Houston deployed left-hander Bennett Sousa as an opener with four left-handed or switch-hitters in the first five spots of the Mets order. It marked Sousa's first start in his 99th major-league appearance. Javier warmed as soon as he began the first inning.

Sousa did not complete it. He issued a leadoff walk to Francisco Lindor. Juan Soto and Bo Bichette both flied out. Carson Benge worked an eight-pitch walk. After getting ahead 0-2 on Jared Young with sliders, Sousa tried another. Young lined it softly into right field for an RBI single.

That proved Sousa's final hitter. He retired one of the three left-handed hitters he faced. Lefties owned a .410 batting average and 1.013 OPS in 46 plate appearances against him entering the day. Sousa became the 18th different pitcher to start a game for the Astros this season, a franchise record.

After taking over with two outs in the first inning, Javier retired 11 of 13 batters to begin his outing. He stranded the exceptions, two singles. Javier did not issue a walk and limited hard contact. But the Mets broke through against him in the fifth.

A misplay helped. With one out, Lindor pulled a drive to right field. Taylor Trammell retreated and leapt near the wall, unnecessarily, missing the ball. Lindor was credited with a double.

Soto, just activated from the injured list, fouled the sixth pitch of his at-bat off the inside of his right leg. Play paused as a trainer checked him. Javier threw two practice pitches during the delay. When Soto did step back in, Javier threw a curveball. Soto lined it into right field for a go-ahead single.

"I feel very confident and very positive in the attack plan that we had," Javier said through an interpreter of the Soto at-bat. "The plan was for him not to hit the ball out of the ballpark and to try to get weak contact. So I felt like we executed that, but unfortunately he won the at-bat there."

Javier retired Bichette on a fly out. But Benge lined a fastball for a single, sending Soto to second. And Young looped an 0-2 sweeper to the right-field corner. Both runners, moving on the 0-2 pitch, scored. Javier faced the Mets lineup twice. He allowed six hits in his 4 ⅓ innings.

"When he gets to that 70-80 (pitch) count, we need to get him through that," Espada said of Javier, who owns a 6.45 ERA in 44 2/3 innings. "I think that's the little hump right now. Stuff looks really good. Once he gets there it just looks like the pitches are starting to flatten up and not really have the depth and the finish that we're looking for."

After Javier's outing, Enyel De Los Santos threw two innings and Teng worked one. The rest of Houston's bullpen should be relatively fresh for Sunday's series finale, in which Ethan Pecko will make his third big-league start.

articles.title: Itauma punches himself out against Hrgovic in world-title fight
articles.summary: Filip Hrgovic shatters Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appears to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight world-title contest in Lon...
articles.body:
Filip Hrgovic ripped up the script and shattered Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appeared to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight contest in London.

Itauma, 21, controlled most of the fight and scored a second-round knockdown but faded as his relentless output caught up with him.

Hrgovic weathered the storm and piled on the pressure in the ninth. With Itauma barely able to stand, his legs unsteady and body swaying before slumping in the corner, his team threw in the towel.

Itauma - who needed medical attention before leaving the arena on a stretcher - had been a heavy favourite after tearing through his first 14 opponents and was spoken about as heavyweight boxing's next superstar.

"He is the best I have been in the ring with, but he needs more experience. I knew I was losing the round, but I knew that I had the pace in my favour. He needs more experience, but he is one of a kind," Hrgovic said.

"From the first round, I saw his gassing out. He started fast. I knew he was going to gas out. I knew when my chance came I needed to push. That is what I did."

With the vacant IBF title on the line, victory would have made Itauma the second-youngest world champion in the division's history.

Instead, his inexperience began to show as his Croatian opponent - an Olympic bronze medallist whose only previous professional defeat came against Daniel Dubois - survived everything Itauma threw at him before completing a remarkable turnaround.

Hrgovic's remarkable turnaround as Itauma shows inexperience

Hrgovic - wearing the red and white checks of his country - made his entrance first to a wall of boos, before the mood inside the O2 Arena flipped as Itauma emerged to a huge roar - taking his time and soaking up the reception.

The crowd had made its allegiances clear after a fiery build-up which included Itauma shoving Hrgovic, the Zagreb man slapping him back and plenty of verbal sparring.

Itauma came out with real intent, landing straight lefts from his southpaw stance. Hrgovic is known for his durability but struggled to keep pace with the Briton's speed early on.

Early in the second, a right hook knocked Hrgovic off-balance and his glove touched the canvas. Oasis star Noel Gallagher and boxing legend Prince Naseem Hamed were among those watching as the crowd gasped at almost every Itauma punch, whether it landed or not.

But by the end of the third, Itauma - who had boxed just 26 professional rounds before his first world-title fight - was already breathing heavily.

There had also been questions over his chin, simply because it had never really been tested. Hrgovic began landing the occasional heavy shot but Itauma took them well and fired straight back.

A fight in the crowd momentarily took attention away from the action in the fifth before an Itauma uppercut in the closing seconds brought the focus back to the ring.

Itauma continued to fire combinations but Hrgovic was barely budging. A huge right landed on the bell in the sixth and another followed in the seventh, yet the Croatian simply walked through them.

The Briton was well ahead but, rather than box his way towards victory, he continued to chase the knockout. A flurry in the eighth backed Hrgovic on to the ropes and had him in trouble, but Itauma was grimacing between exchanges and looking increasingly spent.

By now the danger was clear. Hrgovic came out with renewed purpose in the ninth and landed a thudding right which sent Itauma staggering backwards, almost through the ropes.

The youngster somehow stayed upright but his legs had gone. Hrgovic continued to press and when Itauma slumped into his corner, exhausted and barely able to defend himself, referee Howard Foster waved off the contest as the towel came in.

Hrgovic crashes the party - what next for Itauma?

Hrgovic admitted he had been "outboxed" but leaves London as Croatia's first heavyweight world champion, with Frank Sanchez waiting as the IBF mandatory challenger.

A unification fight could follow, with Daniel Dubois holding the WBO title and set to face Fabio Wardley again in October.

For Itauma, this was supposed to be a coronation.

Instead, he leaves the O2 Arena with questions over whether the step up came too soon.

He has time to rebuild and there will be a strong feeling that, with a little more experience, this night could have ended very differently.

Londoner Dubois was stopped by Joe Joyce as an unbeaten 23-year-old before going on to become a two-time world champion. Itauma has even more time on his side.

"He's an amazing fighter," Hrgovic said. "I am the present. He is definitely the future."

Promoter Frank Warren suggested Itauma was carrying a leg injury in the final round but backed him to return.

"Moses gave everything," he added. "He has to go back to the drawing board and he can come again."

The expectation around Itauma will not disappear entirely overnight but the aura of invincibility has gone.
authors: Kal Sajad - BBC Sport boxing journalist at O2 Arena, London

articles.title: Sunday Matters: Why you need to see the PGA Tour's 2026 Tour Championship finale
articles.summary: It's the final 18 holes of the 2026 PGA Tour season and there's a lot on the line. You don't want to miss this.
articles.body:
After 36 events with 29 different winners, there is just one champion left to be crowned in the PGA Tour's 2026 season. There are 18 holes remaining at the Tour Championship at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, the last of three legs that make up the FedEx Cup Playoffs, and there's a lot on the line ―$10 million, to be exact. That's how much money the man who emerges victorious on Sunday will take home, along with the title of FedEx Cup Champion.

Here's why you need to see the final round of the 2026 Tour Championship. Here's why Sunday Matters :

See the best photos from the 2026 Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta

Here's a look at the top of the leaderboard after 54 holes at the Tour Championship:

There are rollercoaster seasons, and then there's what Viktor Hovland has experienced in 2026. He has had weeks where he's looked like one of the world's best, and he's had weeks where he's struggled immensely. To break it down: Hovland has won once (in a playoff over Scottie Scheffler), he's finished inside the top-15 six times, he's finished outside the top 30 six times, and he's missed four cuts. Up and down, up and down.

Fortunately for Hovland, this is definitely one of those "up" weeks. Pretty good timing considering the Tour Championship features the richest prize on the PGA Tour. Hovland has been flat out excellent at East Lake, carding rounds of 64, 66 and 65 to take the solo lead into the final day. And while everyone knows him as one of the game's premier ball strikers, Hovland has made his money on the greens this week. Even with eight Tour wins and a slew of high finishes throughout his career, Hovland has never ― not once ― led the field in strokes gained putting. Through three rounds at East Lake, he's doing exactly that.

Another thing working in Hovland's favor this week is the fact that he's done this before. He cruised to a five-shot win here in 2023, winning the FedEx Cup in just his fourth full season on Tour. He might not be able to build a cushion that big, given some of the names who will be working to chase him down, but if Hovland can continue putting like he has been all week, he's going to be a very, very tough man to beat on Sunday.

The challengers: Ryan Gerard, Scottie Scheffler

Playing in the final pairing alongside Hovland, 36-hole leader Ryan Gerard managed to keep pace throughout the day, posting a bogey-free, 4-under 66 to enter the final round just one shot off the lead.

Gerard has been one of the Tour's breakout stars over the past year. He burst onto the scene with a win at the Barracuda Championship in July 2025, then got off to a hot start in 2026 with a pair of runner-up finishes in the first two events of the year, the Sony Open in Hawaii and the American Express. He lost in a dramatic playoff against J.T. Poston at the Memorial Tournament, and recorded back-to-back top-10 finishes at the Open Championship and the Rocket Classic.

Gerard now has the chance to establish himself among the best players in the world if he can manage to secure the biggest win of his career at the Tour Championship. If he does, it might raise the eyebrows of one Brandt Snedeker, who will be making his captain's picks for the 2026 Presidents Cup in short order. As if a $10 million prize wasn't motivation enough for Gerard, he has a lot more than money to gain from a stellar performance Sunday.

There are four players tied for third at 12 under, three shots off the lead, but there's one who stands out from that pack. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler has been quietly lurking all week long, posting rounds of 65, 67 and 66 to keep himself right in the mix entering Sunday's final round, where he'll look to win the Tour Championship for a second time.

Scheffler, the 2024 FedEx Cup Champion, won his first start of the year at the American Express, but then suffered through an eight-month winless drought, with five runner-up finishes in that span. He finally broke back into the winner's circle again with an absolutely dominant performance at the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis, where he dusted the field to the tune of an eight-shot victory.

Now, with the PGA Tour Player of the Year race still very much a toss-up, he can strengthen his case and likely win the award for the fifth straight season with a win on Sunday. He'll need a low round to do so, not only because he's three back but because there are so many other big names still in the hunt, but this is Scottie Scheffler we're talking about. When he's chasing, he's dangerous. Hovland, Gerard and the rest of the contenders should fully expect to get Scheffler's best shot in the final round.

There are so many players who could emerge from the pack and make some noise on Sunday, but it's hard to look past the man who's won at East Lake three times before and could add a record fourth FedEx Cup to his trophy case. That would be world No. 2 Rory McIlroy, who looked to be dead in the water after two rounds before making nine birdies en route to a 7-under 63 on Saturday, surging up the leaderboard into a tie for seventh at 10 under.

Sure, he's five shots back, but you might recall the 2022 Tour Championship, when McIlroy began Sunday's final round trailing by four, only to storm back and win the title by one shot. If there was ever a man who epitomizes the cliche "been there, done that," it's Rory McIlroy at East Lake.

Just like Scheffler, he's a dangerous player when he's in full-blown chase mode, and that's exactly the mindset he'll take into Sunday. He came close last week, erasing a five-shot deficit to tie Wyndham Clark's lead on the back nine in the final round of the BMW Championship, only to make a painful bogey on the 71st hole while Clark slammed the door. This time, McIlroy will be looking to finish the job, and it'd be a mistake to count him out.

The best holes in pro golf produce drama, and a long par 3 with a forced carry over water is a great recipe. The ninth at East Lake Golf Club measures as long as 270 yards, with players often taking a long iron, hybrid or even a fairway wood just to hit the green, which slopes from back-to-front and has bunkers guarding it short-right and long-left.

There's really no miss here. Trouble lurks everywhere, and one bad swing can easily dash a player's hopes of winning the Tour Championship before he even reaches the back nine. The strategy is simple: Just hit the green and take your two-putt par. Easier said than done. Through three rounds, No. 9 has played as the second-hardest hole on the course, yielding just two birdies all week.

The FedEx Cup won't be won on the ninth hole Sunday, but it could sure be lost. A poor result can be a real momentum killer, while a good one can propel contenders to the closing stretch with a hop in their step. You'll want to make sure you're tuned in when the final few pairings reach the ninth on Sunday.

The weather: Hot and humid final round in Atlanta

As has been the case for much of these FedEx Cup Playoffs, players will be dealing with hot and humid conditions Sunday in Atlanta. The forecast calls for a high temperature in the upper 80s, with the humidity pushing the heat index well north of 90 degrees. There's a small chance of an isolated thunderstorm in the afternoon, but otherwise, if the players can withstand the heat, it's looking like a day that could yield some low scores, with a light breeze of just 5-10 mph coming from the southeast.
