articles.title: WRC Paraguay: Adrien Fourmaux wins five stages as Sami Pajari strengthens Rally Paraguay lead
articles.summary: Pajari takes a 24.1s lead over Hayden Paddon into Sunday, while Fourmaux cut a 55-second deficit to Elfyn Evans to just 3.3s in the fight for third
articles.body:
Toyota's Sami Pajari edged closer to a third consecutive World Rally Championship victory in Paraguay, while a charging Adrien Fourmaux applied pressure on Elfyn Evans in the fight for third. Pajari increased his 11.9s overnight lead to 24.1s over Hyundai's Hayden Paddon.

Heavy rain was expected to hit the stages but instead storm force winds and a deluge of rain struck the service park causing damage to several team tents. While cooler temperatures lowered the risk of tyre delaminations and punctures that plagued Friday , constantly changing grip conditions remained a challenge.

Hayden Paddon, John Kennard, Hyundai World Rally Team Hyundai i20 N Rally1

Pajari suffered two scares across the nine stages with the Finn fortunate to only suffer a damaged rear wing after running wide into a ditch in stage 11. He reached midday service with a 22.8s lead.

An overshoot on the Bella Vista stage provided another brief scare, but Pajari still outpaced Paddon there and remained composed as tyre management became increasingly important.

"The afternoon was quite exciting even though the conditions were more straight forward but still we were having some small difficulties here and there. The conditions are changing a lot so you have to react quickly," said Pajari.

"It is cool and I need to be happy about leading but I still see many things which can go wrong. If it was Finland or Estonia a 25 second lead is a solid lead but here you could have one stage with bad conditions and you can make a small mistake easily.

"I don't know the latest forecast is exactly for Sunday but we are expecting some rain, where and when and how much, that is the question. We will see."

Paddon struggled to recreate the rhythm that carried him into the lead on Friday, but focused increasingly on preserving tyres and avoiding the trouble that had defined the opening leg.

Adrien Fourmaux, Alexandre Coria, Hyundai Shell Mobis World Rally Team Hyundai i20 N Rally1

Paddon's Hyundai team-mate Fourmaux delivered the drive of the day as the Frenchman set his sights on moving into the victory fight. After starting the day 55.0s behind third-placed Evans, Fourmaux won five of the day's nine stages to end Saturday only 3.3s adrift of Evans, who felt he had been too conservative.

"I'm very proud and I have to accept I'm fighting with the leader of the championship so it was quite nice to take I think 49 seconds and I only had one mistake [a small overshoot in stage 16]," said Fourmaux.

"Clearly the car and me, we had a very good car for these conditions and the set up really helped me. We changed something last night in anticipation of the rain, but it actually suited me very well on the dry so I kept it for the afternoon.

"P3 or even more let's see [what we can do tomorrow]."

Evans conceded that he was unable to find the pace to compete with Fourmaux.

"Adrien had a very strong day and we have been a bit on the conservative side it looks like. I was not able to find the speed as easily. It is going to make it interesting for tomorrow," said Evans. Toyota's Oliver Solberg climbed to fifth after M-Sport-Ford's Josh McErlean slid wide and took down stage-side advertising on the final test, leaving the pair separated by only 6.3s overnight.

Diego Dominguez, Rogelio Peñate, Toyota Gr Yaris Rally2

Home hero Diego Domínguez held seventh overall and leads WRC2, despite spending part of the morning driving without his glasses after accidentally leaving them on the roof of his car. Dominguez's wife sourced a replacement pair from an optician during midday service.

M-Sport-Ford's Jon Armstrong ended the day in eighth, with WRC2 rivals Gus Greensmith and Fau Zaldivar completing the top 10.

Buck Martinez, the former player, manager, and longtime announcer for the Toronto Blue Jays, was one of the first members inducted into the team's new Hall of Excellence on Saturday ahead of their game against the Seattle Mariners.

The Hall of Excellence is a refreshed edition of the team's previous Level of Excellence, which was upgraded with a new physical team museum in the lower level concourse of the Rogers Centre to coincide with the franchise's 50th anniversary.

Martinez is an extremely deserving nominee to be immortalized by the Blue Jays. A catcher during his playing days in the majors, he spent six seasons playing in Toronto, and then joined the broadcast team as a color analyst the year after his retirement.

From there, he would eventually get moved up to manage the Blue Jays for a brief stint, and later called games for the Orioles before returning to the Toronto booth in 2010. He remained with the Blue Jays broadcast team until announcing his retirement ahead of the 2026 season following a series of health issues .

As the banner bearing his name was revealed at the Rogers Centre, Martinez was visibly emotional.

"My induction into the Toronto Blue Jays Hall of Excellence is a very humbling and gratifying honour. Toronto and the entire country of Canada have welcomed me and my family as their own over all these years," Martinez said in a statement shared by the team .

"To the Blue Jays fans across this great country, thank you for all these years of support. I will forever remember all the great memories we have shared along the way. The Toronto Blue Jays, TSN, and Sportsnet have been a huge part of my life and allowed me to enjoy so many wonderful years in Canada."

Martinez also earned a huge cheer from the crowd as he left the field with his signature home run call.

"Swing and a drive. Get up ball! Get outta here! I'm gone."

On the field, the Blue Jays did their part to honor Martinez and the opening day of the new Hall of Excellence, coming back from down 3–0 to defeat the Mariners 4–3.

articles.title: Independent Oakland Ballers minor league club uses metrics, finds winning fan to manage finale
articles.summary: Colt Rosensweig and her two Doberman service dogs, Caris and Curtis, have been in attendance for so much winning at the Oakland Ballers games she has all the...
articles.body:
OAKLAND, Calif. (AP) — Colt Rosensweig and her two Doberman service dogs, Caris and Curtis, have been in attendance for so much winning at the Oakland Ballers games she has all the other fans beat.

And that has earned her chance to be manager for a day.

The Ballers are taking metrics from the diamond and transferring those numbers up into the stands and their fan base – with co-founder Paul Freedman developing their unique version of "WAR," or Wins Above Replacement, which tells how many more victories a player provides a team over someone else who might be called into action instead.

In this case, it's Rosensweig at the top with her "fan value" shining above any other face in the crowd at Raimondi Park. Eligible are those who have attended five or more games and signed up for a "BallerMetrics" profile with the team that uses ticketing data to measure a supporter's impact on the results.

So for Fan Appreciation Day and the final regular-season game against Long Beach Coast on Sunday afternoon, Rosensweig and her pups will be decked out and in the dugout – the 40-year-old professional dog walker working as Ballers manager alongside regular skipper Aaron Miles. He will be Rosensweig's assistant.

"So it turns out that the stats were cumulative, including last year," she explained from her seat during Friday night's after receiving the honor. "Last year other than the last game of the regular season when Aaron was just throwing in a different pitcher every inning, we were undefeated … the dogs were undefeated, except for that last game, and I told Aaron about it and he was like, 'It's my fault.'

"I don't know what the record is, but (Freedman) said I'm 2.4 times luckier than any other fans. That's hilarious."

Each participant's statistics are updated each game, everything from how many runs or stolen bases someone has seen to Ballers' batting average or longest home run when that person is in the ballpark.

"We believe the fans contribute to our success, so we connected the data to make that case," Freedman said.

Among Rosensweig's first questions for Freedman: "Does the manager pick the uniform?" She's partial to the pinstripe pants. But nope, that one's not her call.

She gets to write the lineup, exchange it with the opposing manager and make pitching changes. It also will be Rosensweig's decision when to pinch-hit or sub someone out for the defending Pioneer League champions created by Freedman and co-founder Bryan Carmel two years ago just as the Oakland Athletics were departing the East Bay.

"The one thing we we're not going to have her do is coach third base, just for safety reasons," Freedman said.

Rosensweig suffers from fibromyalgia, a medical condition that causes debilitating pain throughout her body and can come on at any moment. The dogs are harnessed to help her move around, especially after games when she becomes cold, stiff or wobbly and her body just isn't cooperating.

She earned this opportunity even without being a season ticket holder, something that's in the plans for the 2027 season. She purchased flex packages this year and in 2025 with dear friend Catrina "Cat" Christian.

"I'm not wearing a uniform!" she said emphatically, noting she wouldn't mind adding an official Ballers jersey to her collection. "I do own a game-worn Steve Sparks jersey, and if anyone sees that quote and knows who I'm talking about, they should get a prize. He's my favorite ever."

He was a pitcher with five different major league teams over nine years, playing for the Tigers and spending one year in Oakland.

While Rosensweig never played baseball or softball herself, she was a softball scorekeeper during high school at Menlo-Atherton south of San Francisco for a couple of years "then the baseball team's head coach poached me to come do stuff with the guys."

Freedman used his tech background to have some fun developing this stats program. He added an 'f' for fan in front of certain categories, such as "fOBP" for on-base percentage.

"What we did is we took our ticketing data and connected it to the player statistics and then we invited people to claim their profiles," he said. "If you wanted to be anonymous it's all anonymous."

Rosensweig is thrilled — and her numbers are impressive.

The Ballers are 27-10 when she's in attendance, including a 13-game winning streak, and have a team ERA of 4.62, .354 on-base percentage and .472 slugging percentage. She has witnessed 249 runs and 70 homers — Cam Bufford's 425-foot drive being the longest — and four walkoff wins. Six times Oakland has come from behind to win in consecutive games with her there.

Taking part in such a personal way will be beyond meaningful for Rosensweig, who holds fond memories of going to the Coliseum with her father to see their beloved Tigers play the A's beginning when she was a young girl.

Like so many who love and appreciate the loyal Oakland fan base, Rosensweig was hurt by the A's leaving town for West Sacramento as they await the opening of a new ballpark in Las Vegas slated to be done before the 2028 season.

"I love the Ballers. The Ballers have healed my heart from all the awfulness of the A's leaving," she said. "I wasn't exactly an A's fan. We were there to see the Tigers and when the Astros switched to the American League we were there to see the Astros. I've been going to the Coliseum since I was tiny. This is just wholesome."

"She's lucky," Freedman said, "we need her in the stands."

articles.title: Said El Mala speaks on increased expectations associated with Lukas Podolski’s No. 10 shirt
articles.summary: Cologne attacker Said El Mala has admitted feeling the weight of increased expectations after marking his first Bundesliga home appearance in the club’s pres...
articles.body:
Cologne attacker Said El Mala has admitted feeling the weight of increased expectations after marking his first Bundesliga home appearance in the club's prestigious No. 10 shirt with a goal. The 20-year-old struck shortly after halftime as Cologne came from behind to secure a 3-2 victory over TSG Hoffenheim on the opening weekend of the Bundesliga campaign. El Mala's equalizer arrived after he had missed a major opportunity shortly before the break.

Much of Köln's attacking outlook this season rests on their young star. Get German Football News highlighted El Mala's importance to René Wagner's plans in our 2026/27 tactical preview , with the winger ultimately conforming to GGFN expectations by remaining in the cathedral city following an extended summer of transfer speculation. Saturday also represented El Mala's first home match wearing a number carrying considerable symbolic weight in Köln.

The last Effzeh player to wear No. 10 at the RheinEnergieStadion had been club legend Lukas Podolski in May 2012. Asked whether he felt the responsibility that now accompanies his status, El Mala did not attempt to dismiss it.

El Mala on the burden of increased expectations

"I think there's definitely a lot of weight on my shoulders," El Mala told Sky Germany in his post-match interview. "I'd be lying if I said no."

El Mala's missed first-half chance – TSG keeper Oliver Baumann denied him in the 40th minute – only increased the frustration before the breakthrough arrived after the interval. The Krefeld native notched a crucial equalizer six minutes after the restart. A penalty save from Marvin Schwäbe on Max Moerstedt and a brace from the newly arrived Thijs Dallinga ensured that die Geißböcke pulled out a 3-2 home victory.

"I had a little anger inside me and just somehow hit the ball," El Mala added of his deflected equalizer whilst speaking in the mixed zone. "I was a little lucky that it still hit the player [Hoffenheim defender Bernardo]."

"A weight came off my shoulders," El Mala said.

The youngster was later forced off with cramp in the 65th minute, but remained determined to embrace the responsibility accompanying his new shirt number.

"I wear the number with pride," El Mala said. "It's something very special and I work hard for it every day. I want to show the fans that as well."

articles.title: Broncos cut son of 2-time Super Bowl champion 4 days after signing him
articles.summary: The Broncos cut OLB Ron Stone Jr. just days after signing him. The former UFL standout is the son of a two-time Super Bowl champion.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos have kicked off their roster cuts, and a player who just joined the team four days ago has been let go.

The Broncos waived pass rusher Ron Stone Jr., according to multiple reports . Denver had just signed Stone on Tuesday to give them more depth for Friday's preseason finale against the Minnesota Vikings .

"It's added depth that can help take some of the workload off," Denver coach Sean Payton said after the team signed three players ahead of their preseason finale. "It's hard to go into this game and just say, 'Hey, these 40 aren't [playing]'; the stress level then on everyone else kicks up. So it's a challenge whenever you get into this last game, and we'll have a good plan."

Stone is the son of Rob Stone Sr., a two-time Super Bowl champion who was an offensive lineman in the NFL from 1993-2005, spending time with four teams. The elder Stone earned three-time All-Pro nods and two-time Pro Bowl selections during his decorated career.

The younger Stone joined the Broncos after spending this spring with the UFL's Columbus Aviators, totaling 5.5 sacks. Before that, Stone recorded four sacks in nine games with the UFL's Michigan Panthers in 2025. Stone will now hit the NFL's waiver wire. If he clears, Stone could be a candidate to return on Denver's practice squad.

Recently, SB Nation held a fan vote about who the fans think will win the Big Ten and SEC championships this season. The SEC vote was pretty one-sided, with over 56 percent of fans thinking that Georgia will win the SEC. The Big Ten, on the other hand, was much more hotly contested.

Ohio State won the vote, but by a much slimmer margin than Georgia, which had a 25% lead over second-place LSU. Oregon got 38 percent of the vote, while LSU got 31. In third place for both conferences were Texas and Indiana. The Hoosiers got 13 percent of the vote, while Texas got 7 percent.

No matter what, the top of the Big Ten will once again be a dogfight between top tier programs just trying to make history. Between them is Notre Dame in second place at +600 while Texas and Georgia are tied behind the Ducks at +800. Indiana rounds out the top 6 at +900, putting three Big Ten teams in the top 6, more than any other conference.

articles.title: Giants' frustrations with umpires lead to pregame ejection for coach before loss
articles.summary: The Giants, upset by manager Tony Vitello's ejection on Friday, carried their frustration into their doubleheader Saturday as coach Ron Wotus was tossed befo...
articles.body:
A long day at Oracle Park opened with a bang on Saturday, even if it went unnoticed by most fans: Ron Wotus, a non-traveling member of the San Francisco Giants coaching staff, got himself tossed during the lineup card exchange.

The bench coach for the Giants' three championship teams the previous decade, Wotus clearly didn't care for the ejections leveled the previous night. Alan Porter, who was the home-plate umpire Friday night, had tossed manager Tony Vitello and Porter and Wotus exchanged some heated words Saturday until Wotus earned the early shower.

That was the most significant action in the first game of the day-night doubleheader until Lars Nootbaar's grand slam in the seventh off reliever Ryan Walker made up the bulk of the scoring in the Arizona Diamondbacks' 7-1 win. All three baserunners reached via walks, two by starter Matt Wilkinson in an otherwise excellent six-plus inning home debut, and one by Walker. It was the second slam the Giants' bullpen has allowed this week following Eugenio Suárez's drive off Dylan Smith on Wednesday, the centerpiece of the Reds' historic comeback from a six-run deficit in the ninth.

The loss was San Francisco's 81st of the season, giving the team five consecutive non-winning seasons for the first time in franchise history.

The Giants clearly had some strong feelings remaining from Friday night. Wotus refused to be specific about his conversation with Porter but it's safe to assume he was sticking up for Vitello.

a-homered for Fernandez in the 7th. b-singled for Clarke in the 9th. c-flied out for Cavanaugh in the 9th. d-struck out for Furman in the 9th.

E: Hill (2). LOB: Arizona 4, San Francisco 7. 2B: Devers (32). HR: Nootbaar (6), off Walker. RBIs: Nootbaar 4 (26), Perdomo (47), Lawlar (9), Lee (48). SB: Tawa (8).

Runners left in scoring position: Arizona 3 (Lawlar, Carroll, Arenado); San Francisco 2 (Hill, Cavanaugh). RISP: Arizona 4 for 10; San Francisco 1 for 4.

Runners moved up: Vargas. GIDP: Vargas, Carroll, Cavanaugh.

DP: Arizona 1 (Vargas, Perdomo, Tawa); San Francisco 2 (Furman, Koss, Devers; Koss, Furman, Devers).

ABS Challenge: Fernandez (Strike-Overturned to Ball); Waldschmidt (Strike-Overturned to Ball); Wilkinson (Ball-Confirmed); Clarke (Ball-Confirmed).

Umpires: Home, Jim Wolf; First, Jen Pawol; Second, Alex MacKay; Third, Alan Porter.

"I went up there and I asked Alan a few things about last night's game, and at one point he didn't want to discuss it anymore, and I did," Wotus said. "I'm going to leave it at that."

"He walked by and gave me the lineup and said, 'Sorry, I'm done for the day,'" Vitello said. "It took me a second to process it."

There were concerns after Friday's game that the umpires are singling Vitello out because of his lack of pro baseball experience, or, at the very least, that they are quicker with the hook than they might be with others. Both Vitello and director of pitching Frank Anderson, who came with Vitello from the University of Tennessee, have absorbed disparaging comments from umpire this season because of their college background, and Vitello said things "turned personal real quick" with Porter on Friday.

Dusty Baker, on hand for Jeff Kent's jersey retirement before Game 2, said he's unsure if the treatment Vitello is receiving is just because he's a rookie manager or because he came from the college ranks. "Maybe both," Baker said.

With two games Saturday and the same crew in town, Vitello said he had no plans to soft-pedal things. "Might as well be authentic and who you are," he said.

Retired umpire Ed Montague, now a supervisor, chatted with the crew and with Vitello before Game 1 and, Vitello said, "They're human beings. They've got to make calls one way or the other. If (emotions are involved), it's happening unintentionally. I would assume these guys are held to a pretty high standard. … They're trying to get every call correct."

Vitello and the umpires kept their distance Saturday, at least in Game 1. The lineup-card exchange before Game 2 will be watched closely, and the choice for delivering the card will be interesting. Asked if it might be him again, Wotus joked that bench coach Jayce Tingler "won't give me the card."

Wilkinson, 23, worked limited innings in his previous two stints as more of an opener; two in his big-league debut against Cleveland, his former organization, and 3⅔ innings at Boston on Sunday. With the Giants playing two games Saturday and the bullpen covering four innings the night before, Wilkinson needed to go as deep as possible, and he scattered three hits in his first six innings of work, retiring 12 in a row in the middle innings.

"He was great," Vitello said. "I think the fans really got into it and enjoyed watching him pitch in our park. He was outstanding and no disrespect to the Diamondbacks, they didn't really get to him. He just kind of ran out of gas there."

Wilkinson didn't walk a batter until the seventh, when eight of the nine pitches he threw were balls, the result of getting a little too sped up and not adjusting, Wilkinson said. He got a hearty ovation from the Oracle Park crowd, which Wilkinson called, "Pretty cool. Hopefully more to come."

Walker, back up from Triple-A Sacramento just this week, walked Tim Tawa then gave up Nootbaar's slam on a 2-2 fastball at the top of the zone. Typically, Walker throws the four-seam fastball sparingly, just 4% of the time entering Saturday. Last year, he threw two, total.

The Giants' staff, especially the relievers, are under instructions to throw strikes because they've walked far too many - 48 this month from the bullpen entering Game 1, fifth most in the majors. Avoiding walks is laudable, but too many strikes can backfire occasionally, making pitchers a little more predictable.

Left-hander Seth Lonsway, who was called up earlier in the morning, made his big-league debut and struck out Ildemaro Vargas to open the eighth. Lonsway gave up two hits and the Diamondbacks scored an unearned run off him thanks to Turner Hill's error in left, and Arizona scored two more off him in the ninth.

Jung Hoo Lee, the Game 1 bobblehead honoree, drove in San Francisco's run with a single in the eighth.

articles.title: 5-star Miami commit A'mir Sears seizes national spotlight against Bishop Gorman
articles.summary: The next Travis Hunter? Sears, who recently reclassified to the 2027 class, had 67 yards receiving and two TDs, along with 3 INTs on defense.
articles.body:
FORT LAUDERDALE, FL — If you came into this weekend not knowing who A'mir Sears was on an unranked Columbus (FL) team that was supposed to lose to nationally-ranked No. 2 Bishop Gorman (NV), well, you do now.

Sears had his coming out party on national television, catching five passes for 67 yards with a pair of scores, along with three interceptions defense as the Explorers stunned the second-ranked Gaels, 33-28.

"It's not just a title," Sears said. "I'm the No. 1 player in the country."

Sears made that case emphatically, even as Bishop Gorman quarterback Ace Amina tried to test him repeatedly.

And every time Amina (24-42, 334 yards, 3 TD, 3 INT) chose to throw in his direction, it was often either an interception or an incompletion, and that's when Sears missed much of the second half after the second interception due to cramping in both of his legs.

"I can't think of (a performance) I've seen better in person," Columbus head coach Dave Dunn said. "If I can't think of it pretty quick, it means it was probably the best single game performance by a player that I've ever seen."

From the jump, Columbus was ready to go against the Gaels, forcing a three-and-out on the opening drive after multiple lightning delays sent the teams back to the locker room.

Being in Florida, the Explorers might've been used to that. Gorman, not so much.

By the time both teams settled in, it was 20-0 after a pair of touchdowns from Sears in the second quarter. His first interception of Amina set up his first touchdown on the first play of the second quarter.

While Bishop Gorman showed more life in the second half, Spears and the Explorers had an answer for any possible comeback attempt.

Once a second onside kick was recovered by Columbus with under a minute to go in the game, the Explorers could sense it.

"This is the best," Sears said. "I just beat the No. 1 team in the country."

articles.title: Beau Pribula dazzles in Virginia debut as Cavaliers overwhelm NC State 34-8 in season, ACC opener
articles.summary: Transfer quarterback Beau Pribula dazzled in his Virginia debut as the Cavaliers drilled visiting North Carolina State 34-8 in the season and ACC opener for...
articles.body:
CHARLOTTESVILLE, Va. — Transfer quarterback Beau Pribula dazzled in his Virginia debut as the Cavaliers drilled visiting North Carolina State 34-8 in the season and ACC opener for both squads on Saturday at Scott Stadium.

Pribula, who started his career at Penn State and played last season at Missouri, threw for 155 yards and two touchdowns and ran for another 110 yards, becoming the first Virginia quarterback to run for 100 yards in a game since Brennan Armstrong in 2022.

Behind a balanced offense and stifling defense, the Cavaliers jumped out to a 17-0 lead headed into halftime.

Virginia, playing without star linebacker Kam Robinson (knee), had no trouble containing CJ Bailey and the Wolfpack. It opened the game with a pair of three-and-outs and then intercepted a tipped pass on NC State's third possession.

The Wolfpack never threatened. Bailey finished 12 for 23 for 84 yards and an interception. He also lost a red-zone fumble.

North Carolina State: Bailey and the offense could not get going offensively, and the Wolfpack defense was dominated by Virginia's offensive line. State will need to address both those issues if it wants to avoid squandering Bailey's considerable talents.

Virginia: Expectations are running high in Charlottesville, and Saturday's performance will only add to them. Virginia was as advertised: a team that can control the game by running the ball and playing suffocating defense.

Virginia: After an open date, UVA hosts Norfolk State, coached by former Virginia Tech star Michael Vick, in a Friday night game on Sept. 11.

North Carolina State: The Wolfpack will look to bounce back when it faces another Virginia school, FCS Richmond, in Raleigh on Friday, Sept. 11.

articles.title: Ethiopia’s Addisu Gobena storms to a Sydney Marathon record
articles.summary: Ethiopia’s Addisu Gobena surged to a record-breaking victory in the men’s race at the Sydney Marathon on Sunday.  In perfect conditions, Gobena won the hotly...
articles.body:
SYDNEY (AP) — Ethiopia's Addisu Gobena surged to a record-breaking victory in the men's race at the Sydney Marathon on Sunday.

In perfect conditions, Gobena won the hotly contested men's race in two hours four minutes and 42 seconds more than a minute and a half quicker than the previous record on the hilly harborside course which attracted 40,000 competitors from around the world.

The 21-year-old Ethiopian, who was a javelin thrower until 2023, broke away with compatriot Chimdessa Debele Gudeta from the lead pack of six runners inside the final two kilometers and then surged ahead on the downhill finish to the Sydney Opera House to win by four seconds.

Gobena, who finished second behind Hailemaryam Kiros last year, celebrated by punching the air after crossing the finish line.

"I am very happy. Last year I came second, I learnt from my mistake, and I went back home and I worked on my mistake to perform and break the record today," said Gobena through an interpreter.

Lesotho's Tebello Ramakongoana was third in 2:04:57.

The top seven finishers, including Kiros, were all inside Kiros' record time of 2:06:06 set in last year's race.

It was the Sydney Marathon's second year as a major , a list of elite events that includes New York, London, Berlin, Boston, Tokyo and Chicago.

Peres Jepchirchir of Kenya broke the women's field early and raced away to win by more than three minutes as she claimed her fourth marathon major.

Jepchirchir crossed the line in a time of 2:18:31, nine seconds behind Dutch multi-distance star Sidan Hassan's mark set in last year's event.

The Kenyan has now added the Sydney title to her wins in Boston, New York and London.

Compatriot Irene Cheptai was second in 2:22:11, with Shure Demise Ware of Ethiopia another 22 seconds behind in third.

The event was hit by an embarrassing medal mix-up, with a design error resulting in Munich's Allianz Arena being etched onto medals instead of Sydney's Allianz Stadium.

Organizers acknowledged the mistake, which incorrectly depicted a landmark in Germany on medals intended to feature a Sydney landmark.

Daniel Romanchuk of the United States smashed the course record in taking his first Sydney Marathon men's title, as the wheelchair events took place in tandem with the runners

The 28-year-old, who won bronze at the Tokyo Paralympics in 2020, was never threatened as he bested the field early in the race and crossed the line in 1:26:50, more than 30 seconds better than the previous mark.

"I wasn't sure what to expect throughout … I decided to put in a test surge and see what response I got, and I just decided I made a little bit of space, I'll see if I can hold it, and I was able to hold it," Romanchuk said.

Britain's David Weir was second at 1:31:33, with Luo Zingchuan of China two seconds further back in third.

Switzerland's Manuela Schar won the women's event also in a record time of 1:42:04.

Eden Rainbow-Cooper of Britain was second over five minutes behind Schar, with Tatyana McFadden of the United States in third.

"I haven't had the best start to the season. I'm getting older, and it's getting harder, and this is really surprising, and I'm really emotional," Schar said about her margin of victory.

articles.title: 📹 Fans unveil banner for Vasco SAF's prospective new owner
articles.summary: Vasco host Cruzeiro at São Januário this Saturday (29) at 9:20 p.m. (Brasília time) for Matchday 25 of the 2026 Brasileirão.Before kickoff, the Cruz-Maltino...
articles.body:
Vasco host Cruzeiro at São Januário this Saturday (29) at 9:20 p.m. (Brasília time) for Matchday 25 of the 2026 Brasileirão.

Before kickoff, the Cruz-Maltino supporters unveiled a banner in honor of Marcos Lamacchia, the businessman currently "leading" the race to buy the Rio club's SAF.

Also featured on the supporters' banner of the Giant of the Hill was José Roberto Lamacchia, Marcos' father and the husband of Palmeiras president Leila Pereira.

In addition to the banner, Vasco fans sang: "Olê lê, olá lá, Lamacchia is coming and things are going to heat up!"

👀 Sale of the SAF and the Pedrinho x Bap feud

The imminent sale of 90% of Vasco's SAF to businessman Marcos Lamacchia has sparked a series of clashes between Pedrinho, president of the Giant of the Hill, and Luiz Eduardo Baptista, president of archrivals Flamengo.

Bap alleges "cross-ownership" and a conflict of interest, arguing that the family relationship could amount to undue influence by Leila Pereira (Marcos Lamacchia's stepmother) over two Brasileirão clubs, which would be prohibited under financial fair play rules and Brazilian football regulations.

The Rubro-Negro chief has already indicated that he will take the matter to court and has contacted the regulatory agency (ANRESF) and the CBF in an attempt to block the transaction.

On the other side, Pedrinho has pushed back against the criticism, calling Bap's stance a "persecution" of Vasco and defending the legality of the deal and its importance for the club's financial recovery.

While the courts analyze the sale process, Vasco are seeking approval for a DIP loan worth R$150 million, requested urgently to cover immediate obligations during judicial recovery.

However, the judge has kept the freeze on that credit line, questioning financial projections and requesting further clarification before making a decision.

Vasco are languishing in second-to-last place with just 22 points and need to start winning again to avoid getting into even deeper trouble in the relegation battle.

Cruzeiro, meanwhile, sit fifth in the table with 39 points and are chasing a fifth straight league win to break into the top four.

Both teams are involved in the Copa do Brasil quarterfinals.

In the first leg, the Cruz-Maltino beat Vitória 1-0 at São Januário and will play for a draw at Barradão next Wednesday (2) to reach the semifinals.

A Raposa, meanwhile, drew 1-1 with Atlético-MG in the first leg and will need to beat their rivals at Arena MRV next Tuesday (1) to advance.

articles.title: Federer Enters Tennis Hall Of Fame As Contemporaries Play US Open
articles.summary: Roger Federer Entered the International Tennis Hall Of Fame as contemporaries Novak Djokovic, Stan Wawrinka, Serena Williams, and Venus Williams, play in the...
articles.body:
Roger Federer was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame today, along with tennis commentator Mary Carillo. Federer gave an emotional and tearful speech during his induction ceremony in Newport, Rhode Island.

He enters the Hall of Fame while several players from his era are in the main draw of the 2026 U.S. Open.

Since retiring in 2022 , Federer has watched Venus Williams, 46, return from inactive to active and Serena Williams, 44, evolve back into tennis. His compatriot Stan Wawrinka, 41, and friend Gael Monfils, who turns 40 on September 1, are retiring this year, but are also playing in the U.S. Open.

During a press conference leading up to the "Roger Federer: An Icon Returns to New York" night at the U.S. Open, a reporter asked Federer if he ever considered returning to tennis, maybe taking a wildcard to play at the U.S. Open. Federer responded with a definitive no.

"No, no, no, no, no, not at all," Federer said, while laughing. "God, there's way too many obstacles, and I, I'm too busy. I'm barely finding time to play any exos (exhibitions), you know. So imagine a tour, and the body is done. . . I'm very happy how I'm feeling. So all good, and just a fan now, just enjoying watching."

Federer has approached his retirement the same way he did his playing career, with clarity and class.

Federer Remains The Wealthiest Of The Big Three

Federer's claim to GOAT status slipped away when Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic surpassed him in Majors won. He has a losing record against both. Yet Federer is the GLOAT, greatest loved of all time.

Despite trailing Nadal and Djokovic in Majors and career prize money , Federer outpaced them in endorsements and wealth.

Until recently, Federer was a billionaire , having amassed a fortune almost double what Nadal earned during his career. The only former professional tennis player with a higher net worth than Federer is Ion Tiriac, who made his money in financial services, real estate, autos, and more after his playing career.

"I think the charitable work I think for anyone who's in it and can donate their time or money or expertise or just have a conversation about it and think how we can always help each other out or mentor, et cetera, I think it's important," Federer said at a press conference the day before his induction. "For me, children have always been front and center. How can I inspire the next generation on the tennis court, but also with the Roger Federer Foundation, how much can we make a difference in as many kids' lives as possible to have quality education in places where maybe that is not always the case?"

Federer Reflects On His Impact On The Game

"I hope I represented the sport well, that they liked to watch me play or liked watching my highlights down the road," said Federer. "But more so, that maybe I helped drive the sport in the right direction, together with, you know, the leaders of the sport, maybe on the ATP side or with the slams."

During the Hall of Fame weekend interview, Patrick McEnroe asked Federer if he'd consider coaching, like Andy Murray, Andre Agassi and Boris Becker have done.

"I guess with Laver Cup down the road maybe the captain role is definitely something I could consider, for sure," said Federer. "Coaching at the minute, no, just because I'm too busy, and kids need my undivided attention. Plus, I have too many projects. I love my time and my life with my wife, so I don't want to change that at the minute, but never say never."

Djokovic congratulated Federer on his induction into the Hall of Fame in a video tribute played during the U.S. Open.

"What you have achieved, what you represented and still represent for the sport of tennis and sport in general is something truly incredible and remarkable," Djokovic said. "Thank you for being such a great ambassador for our sport. Hopefully you will have an amazing day with your family, celebrating your amazing career."

Soon, Djokovic, Wawrinka, Venus and Serena will be back on the court at the U.S. Open. Meanwhile, Federer's legacy is on permanent display in the Tennis Hall of Fame, awaiting their arrival.

articles.title: Dodgers Should Pounce on Luis Robert Jr. After Stunning Waiver Development
articles.summary: A possible solution for the Los Angeles Dodgers' offensive woes may have hit the waiver wire in the form of Luis Robert Jr.
articles.body:
A possible solution for the Los Angeles Dodgers' offensive woes may have hit the waiver wire in the form of Luis Robert Jr.

Robert Jr. broke out years ago with the Chicago White Sox as one of the most promising players in the big leagues in the early 2020s, but in the last few seasons, he has experienced a fall from grace.

He was finally traded away from Chicago over the offseason to the Mets, who needed a veteran outfielder, but his fresh start has not gone as he expected.

Now, to save some money, the Mets put Robert Jr. on waivers to see if another team will pick him up.

Robert Jr. has a $20 million team option for the 2027 season, and $5 million left on his deal in terms of guarantees.

He is owed $3 million in salary and a $2 million buyout fee.

This season, he is hitting .228 with 10 home runs and 23 RBIs, along with two stolen bases and a .715 OPS.

However, things have been better for the Cuban lately. He is hitting .279/.373/.651 over his 15 games, and things look even better over his last seven games — .304/.407/.696.

The turning point came after the trade deadline, when he was available, but teams were reluctant to deal for him because of his low production heading into the trade window.

Seemingly, all he needed was some time to recover from a back injury that he had just returned from in the middle of July.

Why the Dodgers could use Luis Robert Jr.

He hits right-handed, like the Dodgers' current backup outfield bat, Alex Call, but Robert Jr. has the talent to hit a different level.

This year, the longtime center fielder played left field and has also played right field at times. His defense has taken a big step up this year compared to previous years, and his athleticism gives him the ability to be a big-time glove.

Robert Jr. has the ability to help the depth of the Dodgers and give their two struggling outfielders some competition as well.

He comes at a somewhat high cost given his season-long production, but if he can keep hitting the ball as he has recently, he would immediately help the offense.

As everyone knows, the Dodgers spare no expense if it can help the team win games, and it is hard to argue Robert Jr. wouldn't be an upgrade.
